account: It is day 1 at 13:00, and I have returned to the town hall for council letters. The secretary is nearby; I have not yet asked what correspondence awaits. This morning the builder reported the west-bank roads passable, with no identified defects or repair costs. I have authorized no repair spending; any later proposal needs itemized prices and approval. The unusual item today is a vague rumour of changes at the bridge or port. The builder mentioned a child's remark, and the neighbour and freight also asked about it, but I have seen no change and heard no definite proposal or reliable explanation of its purpose. I should not treat repetition as confirmation. At the scheduled mill inspection I found 128 hay bales in the sale chest and left them untouched. That establishes visible stock, not grain quality or delivery requirements. Neither the neighbour nor freight could identify the stock manager or confirm a shortage or delivery order. Freight said the warehouse was empty when last checked, offered storage and transport, and planned to ask the baker about grain needs before moving anything. This appears to be checking for ordinary supply work, not evidence of a planned bridge or port change. The neighbour expects me for tea at the dockside cottage at three. For now my business is council correspondence, and I still need definite information before drawing conclusions about the rumours.
